## AI app factory

This repository is worked on through the AI app factory. Its engine is installed outside the repository; everything it keeps here is under `.factory/` (settings in `.factory/config.json`, agent addenda, lessons, architecture policy, test plans, test stack scenarios). Run it as `factory <command>`; when `factory` is not on your PATH, use `.factory/bin/factory <command>`.

- To run stories through the whole pipeline: `factory implement run <KEY>...` (`--parallel N` runs several at once). It starts the implementer in each story's own worktree and branch; you don't need the steps below.
- When you start implementing a story by hand, run `factory start <KEY>`.
- When your line of work for that story is complete, run `factory done` before you finish. The Stop hook then runs the architecture review. If it blocks with findings, fix them and finish again; tests are written automatically after approval.
- Stories, epics, spikes and mockups are tickets on the story board, cached in `.factory/state/board/<KEY>/`. Ignore that cache except for the story handed to the pipeline (`factory start <KEY>` or `factory implement run`). A PreToolUse hook enforces this.
- Do not edit `.factory/` or the files listed in `.factory/manifest.json` while implementing a story: they belong to the factory, not to the application. Change generated files through their source and `factory render`. `factory check` fails when a generated file was edited by hand.
- Tests the pipeline writes live in the application's own test tree and are tagged with their story; treat them like any other test.

## graphify

This project has a knowledge graph at `graphify-out/` (built locally; run `factory graphify-build` when `graphify-out/graph.json` is missing).

- Run `graphify query "<question>"` before your first grep, search or source-file read for a codebase question, and put this rule in every subagent prompt that explores code. Read raw files only for lines the graph or an earlier read already located.
- Use `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` for relationships and `graphify explain "<concept>"` for focused concepts.
- After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (no API cost).

## Code intelligence (LSP)

The MCP server `lsp` exposes this repository's language servers. Use it for precise work at code you already located:

- Before changing existing code, confirm it: `lsp_goto_definition` and `lsp_hover` for the real definition and signature, `lsp_find_references` for every caller before you change a signature or behavior.
- After every edit, run `lsp_diagnostics` on the edited files.
- Rename with `lsp_rename` (`dry_run: true` first) instead of search and replace.
- Paths are absolute and inside your own checkout; line and column are 1-indexed. When a call answers "language server unavailable", do not retry in a loop: search instead.
